Glossary & Methodology

What is "Cumulative Returns Volatility Matched To Benchmark"?

This metric is a mathematical way to compare the performance of different assets by leveling the playing field in terms of risk (volatility). We measure how volatile an asset is compared to the benchmark (Nifty 50). If a stock is twice as volatile as the Nifty 50, its daily returns are mathematically halved to match the benchmark's risk profile. Conversely, if an asset is half as volatile, its returns are doubled. "Cumulative Returns" means we track the compounded growth of these adjusted daily returns starting from a base value of 100.

Raw stock: wild, high-volatility swings
Vol-matched: same trend, smoothed to benchmark risk

Why is it different from the actual stock price?

  • Raw Stock Price ignores risk: Actual price returns show absolute growth but ignore how much risk was taken to get there.
  • Volatility Matching reveals Risk-Adjusted Momentum: This metric tells you: "If this stock had the exact same risk (smoothness) as the overall market, what would its return actually be?"
  • The Benefit: Volatility matching penalizes wild swings and rewards assets that deliver smooth, consistent uptrends (true alpha).
  • Sector averages: computed as the average of raw (unmatched) stock returns within a sector, then vol-matched as a single series.

Risk Metrics Explained

  • Sharpe Ratio: Return earned per unit of total volatility, adjusted for a ~6.5% risk-free rate. Higher is better; above 1.0 is generally considered good, above 2.0 excellent.
  • Sortino Ratio: Like Sharpe, but only penalizes downside volatility — better reflects "bad" risk since upside swings aren't penalized.
  • Max Drawdown: The largest peak-to-trough decline over the period, on the vol-matched series. Tells you the worst pain you'd have sat through.
  • Beta (proxy): Ratio of the stock's raw volatility to the benchmark's — a rough stand-in for market beta. >1 means historically more volatile than Nifty 50.
  • Raw Vol %: The stock's actual annualized volatility before any vol-matching was applied — tells you how much leverage/de-leverage was needed.
  • Leverage: The multiplier applied to raw returns to match benchmark volatility (capped between 0.1x–10x).
